data.one_liner: Automatically adapt Flutter app UI to different screen sizes and breakpoints.
data.what_it_does: Provides widgets and utilities to make Flutter apps responsive. It includes breakpoint management, responsive values, grids, row/column switches, and auto-scaling capabilities for mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts.
use_when: You need to build layouts that adapt to multiple screen sizes from mobile to 4K desktop.
You want to manage breakpoints globally using MaterialApp or CupertinoApp builders.
You require conditional UI rendering based on screen size or orientation.
avoid_when: You prefer implementing custom LayoutBuilder and MediaQuery logic manually for every screen.
You are building a fixed-size application that will never run on varying form factors.
strengths: Simplifies cross-platform responsive design with predefined breakpoints and helper widgets.
Offers both resizing and proportional auto-scaling features.
Includes helpful layout components like ResponsiveRowColumn and ResponsiveGridView.
weaknesses: Legacy ResponsiveWrapper has been deprecated, requiring migration to ResponsiveBreakpoints.
Auto-scaling can occasionally make text or UI elements look overly large on extremely wide viewports if not configured properly.
data.setup_notes: Add ResponsiveBreakpoints.builder to your MaterialApp or CupertinoApp builder function.

alternatives.name: responsive_builder
alternatives.why_pick_it: Alternative approach to building responsive UIs with dedicated screen type builders.

alternatives.why_pick_it: Alternative utility focused on scaling UI elements based on screen width and height percentages.
